name: Community Service & Civic Engagement

objectives.text: Describe ways students can serve their local community, such as helping at a food drive or cleaning up a park
Identify local organizations that meet community needs, such as food pantries, extension offices, 4-H clubs, and fair boards
Explain why people serve their neighbors and care for shared community resources
Explain how a chapter community service project benefits people beyond the chapter
Describe how local governing bodies such as county commissions, school boards, and soil and water conservation districts make decisions that affect agriculture and natural resources
Explain ways citizens take part in local decision making, such as attending public meetings, giving public comment, and voting
Participate in a chapter-organized community service project and reflect in writing on what was learned and who was served
Explain how FFA offices, community service, leadership conferences, and FFA programs such as National Day of Service build leadership and citizenship skills
Identify community service opportunities available through local organizations, agribusinesses, and community events
Conduct a community needs assessment using surveys, interviews, or local data to identify a need the chapter could address
Plan a community service project with goals, a timeline, a budget, member roles, and safety considerations that addresses an identified local need
Develop a personal plan for ongoing involvement in community service, such as volunteering regularly or joining a community committee
Design a service-learning SAE that meets a community need and documents hours, activities, and outcomes in an SAE record book
Prepare a grant application, such as an FFA Living to Serve grant, to fund a chapter community service project
Assess opportunities to serve on community boards, committees, and agricultural organizations and develop strategies for taking part in them
Lead a team of members in organizing and carrying out a community service project using strategies that keep members engaged toward shared goals
Build partnerships with businesses, agencies, and civic groups to share resources for a community service project
Present a proposal for a community improvement project to a local governing body or stakeholder group
Analyze a local agricultural or natural resource issue and propose ways citizens and community groups can improve how decisions about it are made
Create a plan to gather feedback from team members and community stakeholders after completing a service project
Evaluate the impact of a community service initiative using stakeholder feedback and propose ways to improve and sustain it

changes: Kept all six original competencies, rewording several (grade 8 now includes a written reflection, grade 11 now names team engagement, grade 12 now uses stakeholder feedback). Added elementary and middle objectives on local service organizations, motives for service, and how local governing bodies and citizens make decisions, so the civic engagement half of the sub-topic is covered. Added high school objectives on FFA citizenship programs, identifying service opportunities, needs assessment, a personal service plan, service-learning SAE, grant writing such as Living to Serve, serving on boards and committees, community partnerships, presenting proposals to governing bodies, analyzing local decision making, and post-project feedback planning. Mapped AFNR Career Ready Practice and FPS codes only where the objective teaches the standard. Objectives below grade 9 carry no standards. Advocacy, CDE, and networking content was left to the sibling sub-topics.
